auth-worker-contract.description: The Auth Worker Contract: what every program may rely on without running the Auth Worker (API base path, issuer, JWKS URL, what an Access Token says, the User, and the PagesContext the Worker hands its pages). Plain TypeScript, no dependencies.

database.description: Primary Database providers the consumer hands to the Auth Worker. A future non-SQLite dialect would be a second module graph here.

sqlite.description: D1 runtime database, D1 deployment resource, and memory database are independent doors built on separate private schema and migration modules.

primitives.description: The pages' own copies of the shadcn primitives and the class-name helper the screens are built from

theme.description: The pages' light and dark theme: one cookie the server reads before the first paint and the browser keeps in step
createTheme is the browser's door; tanstack-start reads the theme cookie on the server.

screens.description: The Auth Worker's screens as pure views: state in, actions out

auth-screens.description: The Auth Worker's four screens (Home Page, Login Screen, Consent Screen, Device Screen) as pure views: state in, actions out, one frame, one loader, and one account switcher for the browser's Signed-in Accounts

pages.description: What the Auth Worker's pages show: connects the Worker's data to the auth screens and owns no markup of its own.

Four page doors (Home Page, Login Screen, Consent Screen, Device Screen) over one same-origin Better Auth API, the User's Sessions and Grants, the browser's Signed-in Accounts, and one rule for which screen a visitor may see.

app.description: The pages app: a TanStack Start site whose routes render the pages, built by Vite and embedded into the worker door by scripts/bundle-app.mts

worker.description: createAuthWorker(config) assembles Better Auth over a consumer-provided Primary Database (Cookie Cache, Google, Admin, Device Login, optional Signed-in Accounts, Dash, Authorization Server Role, User Admission Policy, origins and cookies) and serves the pages app the built door embeds

vanilla.description: Consumer Backend doors with no framework: Server-Side Verification of a Session, local verification of an Access Token, and the MCP Server door, all speaking one Principal

effect.description: The vanilla doors lifted into Effect: one Current Auth that resolves a request to a Principal (its live Resolver, which asks the Auth Worker through better-auth, kept apart so a device-only backend never bundles it), and an Auth Cannotation per Sibling (RPC, HTTP API), each split into a browser-safe Declaration and its Server Implementation

rpc.description: The RPC Auth Cannotation: a private Cannotation, the Declaration contract code imports, and the Server Implementation that verifies each call and relays refreshed cookies.

http-api.description: The HTTP API Auth Cannotation: a private Cannotation, the Declaration contract code imports, and the Server Implementation that verifies each request.

accounts.description: A First-Party app's Signed-in Accounts as one Effect service, Auth, with one target per platform: live against the Auth Worker in a browser, local with Local Accounts kept in a StdTable, and expo, where each User signs in as the app's OAuth client and keeps their own tokens on the phone; plus fetch signed as one account

The Auth service and its targets. The platform-free door (index.ts) gathers the service, local and signed; live (better-auth's browser client) and expo are doors of their own, so a phone bundles none of the browser's code and the browser none of Expo's.

client-app.description: An app on the toolkits: createApp opens and closes the app's backend store and session store with the Gate, on the platform web-toolkit or expo-toolkit gives (AppPlatform), and deletes a signed-out user's copy (copyName)

gate.description: The Gate: runs sign-in on one device for any app on any platform. It keeps the app on a Backend, holds the Backend Lifetime and the Active Account's Session Lifetime, opens a known account first and confirms it behind, remembers the Signed-in Accounts in a table of its own, stops at an Account Lost, and leaves Gate Notices. No platform code: the platform is handed in. react is its React side, the same on every platform.

gate.ts runs one Backend at a time and the machine on it, with the platform handed in; domain is the machine, the check and the services it asks; memory is the table the Gate remembers in; platform is what a platform hands in; react is SignedIn, SignedOut and the hooks.

cli.description: Effect-only: a First-Party CLI's Device Login, its Session Store, and the Session on every RPC call

auth-worker.description: The Auth Worker and everything it serves. The worker reads the contract; the pages app renders the pages, and the pages show the screens; the Primary Database is handed to the worker by the consumer. The worker and the app meet at build time, never through an import.

consumer-backend.description: A Consumer Backend asking the Auth Worker who is calling: verify with no framework, then optionally lift the result into Effect.

clients.description: First-Party programs holding a Session: the browser's Auth and the CLI, each reading only the contract.
